title: Descent and projectivity of finite normalized blowup towers
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian quasi-excellent normal separated scheme [def-exc-excellent-ring], [pqf-def-locnoeth], and let $u:U\to X$ be a surjective quasi-compact etale morphism with $U$ Noetherian. A finite normalized blowup tower consists of finitely many ordered steps, each the ordinary blowup of a coherent ideal with nowhere dense zero set [def-nagata-global-blowup], followed by componentwise normalization in the function fields [def-sc-normalization]. The tower remembers the ideal centers, not only the morphisms. Given such a tower on $U$, suppose that its two scheme pullbacks to $U\times_XU$ are canonically isomorphic as towers with the same number of stages and with their center ideals identified, and that these identifications satisfy the cocycle on $U\times_XU\times_XU$. Then there is a unique such tower on $X$ inducing the given tower and descent datum, up to unique compatible isomorphism. Equality of ideal centers, or equality of two towers with synchronized stages, can be checked after any jointly surjective family of flat morphisms on each stage. Etale pullback commutes with every normalized blowup in these towers.

Each normalization in any such tower over $X$ is finite. All stages are Noetherian, normal and quasi-excellent; the final composite is projective in the projective-bundle sense [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism], of finite type, and is an isomorphism outside the images of the centers. If $X$ is integral then every stage is integral and the tower induces the identity on the common dense open and on its function field. An action on a tower of $U$ compatible with the descent datum descends. The same assertions about finiteness, projectivity and integrality hold for a tower already given on $X$, without a cover.

source.place: VIII 2.2.1--2.2.4 and 3.4.8, printed pp.89--90,111; 5.5.3--5.5.5, printed pp.128--129 (descent of the ordered centers); Stacks Tags 035S (morphisms.tex, lemma-nagata-normalization), 02NS (divisors.tex, lemma-blowing-up-projective), 0C4P (morphisms.tex, lemma-composition-projective).

proof.text: First establish the geometry for a tower already on a normal Noetherian quasi-excellent base $S$, without assuming it separated. Its finitely many irreducible components are open normal integral schemes, by the finite-components and normal-components lemmas. On each component the center ideal is nonzero: its zero set contains no generic point. The integral-blowup lemma makes the ordinary blowup integral on that component. Blowup restricts to these open components by flat base change. For projectivity on all of $S$, the Rees-presentation lemma gives the surjection $\operatorname{Sym}(I)\twoheadrightarrow\bigoplus I^n$ and identifies the blowup with the latter's relative Proj. Relative-Proj functoriality gives a closed immersion into $\mathbf P_S(I)$, exactly projectivity in the stipulated convention. Thus the ordinary blowup $B$ is reduced and has one integral component over each component of $S$. The empty base gives the empty blowup.

source.place: VIII 2.2.1--2.2.5, pp.90--91; ordinary geometry: Stacks Tags 0804, 02ND, 02NS (divisors.tex, lemma-blowing-up-affine, lemma-blow-up-integral-scheme, lemma-blowing-up-projective)

proof.text:
Projectivity makes $B	o S$ proper and of finite type. Since $S$ is quasi-compact, its source is quasi-compact: take a finite affine cover of $S$ and the finite affine inverse-image covers in the definition of finite type. Quasi-excellent finite-type stability therefore makes $B$ Noetherian and quasi-excellent. On an affine $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset B$, quasi-excellence makes $A$ Nagata. For every minimal prime $\mathfrak p_j$ of $A$, the definition of Nagata says $A/\mathfrak p_j$ is Japanese. Apply its finite-normalization assertion to the degree-one field extension $K_j/K_j$, where $K_j=\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak p_j)$. The integral closure $A'_j$ is finite over $A/\mathfrak p_j$, hence over $A$. The affine normalization formula identifies $
u^{-1}(\operatorname{Spec}A)$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(\prod_j A'_j)$. This finite product is a finite $A$-module (combine the finitely many generating sets), so $
u:B^
u	o B$ is finite by definition. This proves finiteness using quasi-excellence, without adding universal catenarity.

The finite map $B^
u	o B$ is projective by the finite-projective-bundle lemma, hence proper and of finite type. Applying quasi-excellent finite-type stability again shows that $B^
u$ is Noetherian and quasi-excellent; normality is the normalization generic-properties lemma. A locally Noetherian scheme is quasi-separated, so both $B$ and $S$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The projective-bundle composition lemma applies to $B^
u	o B	o S$. Induct on the number of stages, starting with $S$ and its identity: every stage is normal Noetherian quasi-excellent, every normalization is finite, and every partial composite is projective. In the induction step compose the projective next arrow with the preceding projective composite, whose target $S$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The identity is the projective bundle $\mathbf P_S(\mathcal O_S)=S$. The finite-type clause follows from projectivity, since projective morphisms are proper and proper morphisms are of finite type, including for the length-zero tower.

Each ordinary blowup is the identity on the complement of its center. On each integral component this nonempty open is dense, since it contains its generic point; the blowup source is integral by step 1. Normalization induces a bijection on component generic points with identical residue fields. On the inverse image of the center complement it is an isomorphism: normalization commutes with restriction to an open, and a normal scheme with locally finitely many components has trivial normalization. Thus each normalized arrow is birational on each component. For a finite tower on $X$, let $Z$ be the union of the images in $X$ of all the centers. Each image is closed, since the partial composite is projective and hence proper. It contains no generic point of $X$: inductively that generic point has a single generic preimage, outside the next center. Thus $Z$ is nowhere dense and every stage is the identity over the common dense open $X\setminus Z$. When $X$ is integral, step 1 and the generic-point bijection show every stage integral; the function-field identifications are the identity through this common open. These arguments also cover empty centers and the length-zero tower.

source.place: VIII 2.1.1--2.1.3 and 2.2.1--2.2.5, pp.86--87,90; Stacks Tags 035Q, 07TD, 0H7D, 01OF (blowup complement)

proof.text: Record rigidity needed for comparing the supplied datum with the reconstructed one. A normalized blowup over a normal Noetherian quasi-excellent $S$ has no nonidentity $S$-automorphism. Work over an affine open $V\subset S$. Its normalized blowup is separated as an absolute scheme, since it is projective over the affine scheme $V$. It is normal, with finitely many integral open components; the inverse image of the center complement is dense in every component by step 4. It is schematically dense: on an affine open in an integral component, restriction of functions to any dense open is injective, since a function vanishing there has a zero locus containing a dense subset and therefore lies in every prime, hence is zero in the domain. The agree-on-dense-open lemma now makes an automorphism the identity, since it is the identity over the center complement. Glue over the affine opens of $S$. Induction on stages gives rigidity for the whole tower with its base fixed. This local argument also works when $S=U$ is not separated.

For an etale $v:T\to S$, the ordinary blowup comparison is an isomorphism because $v$ is flat. The induced map between ordinary blowups is the base change of $v$, hence etale. Both blowups are locally Noetherian: this is affine-local finite-type stability over their locally Noetherian bases. The componentwise-normalization smooth-pullback lemma, in its explicit etale case, identifies their normalizations. Combining these two comparisons identifies the normalized blowup of the extended ideal with the scheme pullback of the original normalized blowup. Repeating at each ordered stage proves etale compatibility for towers. The comparisons respect identity maps and composition: the blowup comparison is defined by coefficient pullback on the Rees algebras, and the normalization comparison is the unique isomorphism over the pulled-back ordinary blowup. No assertion of normalization commuting with arbitrary flat base change is used. In particular $U$ and the overlap stages are normal by smooth normal ascent, since etale maps are smooth; quasi-excellence and local Noetherianity ascend by finite-type stability. Their quasi-compact covers are Noetherian. These checks allow the same rigidity and construction arguments over the overlap bases.

source.place: VIII Lemma 2.2.9 and 2.2.11, p.91; Stacks Tags 0805 (flat blowup base change), 07TD (lemma-normalization-and-smooth)

proof.text: For later use, ideal equality is detected by ANY jointly surjective flat family $T_a\to S$. At $s\in S$ choose $t\in T_a$ above it. The flat local homomorphism $A=\mathcal O_{S,s}\to B=\mathcal O_{T_a,t}$ is faithfully flat. For ideals $I,J\subset A$ with $IB=JB$, every $x\in I$ maps to zero in $B/JB$. Apply universal injectivity to $A/J$: its map into $(A/J)\otimes_A B=B/JB$ is injective, so $x\in J$. Interchange $I,J$. Flat pullback is exact, hence its ideal submodule is precisely the extended ideal in $B$; this justifies using these stalk equalities. Equality at all stalks is equality of subsheaves, since membership in a subsheaf is local. The same faithful-flat argument shows a map of modules with injective pullback is injective: apply it to each element of its kernel. No quasi-compactness of the family is needed for these detection assertions.

source.place: VIII Corollary 5.5.3, pp.128--129 (centers detected faithfully flat); Stacks Tags 05CK (lemma-faithfully-flat-universally-injective), 00HR (flat local faithful flatness)

proof.text: Descend centers and construct the tower by induction. Write $U_0=U$, $X_0=X$, and keep the original index set $0,\ldots,n$. Suppose $X_i$ and the comparison $U_i\simeq U\times_X X_i$ have been constructed and induce the given datum through stage $i$; this is true for $i=0$. The map $u_i:U_i\to X_i$ is a singleton fpqc cover, being the base change of the quasi-compact surjective flat map $u$. Apply quasi-coherent fpqc descent to the next center $J_i$ and its inclusion $J_i\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_{U_i}$; the given identification of centers says exactly that this inclusion respects the datum. Fully faithful descent gives a map $M_i\to\mathcal O_{X_i}$, and step 7 makes it injective. Its image $I_i$ is therefore a quasi-coherent ideal with pullback $J_i$. On an affine open of the Noetherian $X_i$, it is a submodule of the finite module $A$, hence finitely generated by the Noetherian-submodule lemma. The coherent/finite-type criterion makes $I_i$ coherent. Its zero set is nowhere dense: for each generic point $\eta$ of $X_i$, $\mathcal O_{X_i,\eta}$ is a field. A point $t$ of the surjective cover over $\eta$ is generic: every generalization of $t$ maps to $\eta$, while the etale fibre over $\eta$ is zero-dimensional and has no proper generalizations. Thus $J_i$ is the unit ideal at $t$. Thus $I_i$ cannot be zero at $\eta$ and is the unit ideal there.

source.place: VIII 2.2.11, p.91 and 5.5.5, p.129; Stacks Tag 023T (proposition-fpqc-descent-quasi-coherent), 01XZ (coherent finite-type criterion)

proof.text: Set $X_{i+1}=\operatorname{Bl}_{I_i}(X_i)^\nu$. Steps 1--3 make it a normal Noetherian quasi-excellent next stage, with all the required geometry. Step 6 identifies $U\times_X X_{i+1}$ with the original normalized blowup of $J_i$, namely $U_{i+1}$. On the overlap the supplied descent isomorphism and the canonical comparison are isomorphisms over the same stage-$i$ scheme, identifying the same center. Their difference is an automorphism of its normalized blowup, so it is the identity by step 5. Consequently the comparison realizes the prescribed datum, not just its underlying object. This completes the induction. The full-faithfulness clause of module descent makes the descended ideal and inclusion unique at each stage; the functorial blowup and normalization constructions then give the comparison with any other descended tower, unique by step 5. Hence the resulting tower is unique up to unique compatible isomorphism.

For synchronized towers already on $X$, apply step 7 at the first centers to get their equality. Their normalized blowups are then the same construction, up to the unique comparison of step 5. Proceed to the next identified stage and repeat; the prescribed common stage set is essential. This proves the stated flat-family test. Here only equality of the pulled-back ideal subsheaves on each stage is tested; it does not require defining normalized blowup pullback for an arbitrary flat map. For an action on the tower over $U$ compatible with the descent datum (in particular the finite-group actions in the source), descend each of its automorphisms stage by stage along $u_i$ using fpqc descent of scheme morphisms. Descend its inverse too. Both composites, the action multiplication law, its identity law, compatibility with arrows, and preservation of the center inclusions hold after the covering; uniqueness of descended morphisms and the ideal test make them hold downstairs. Thus this is an action on the descended tower. For a scheme-valued group action, apply the same morphism descent to the action map along the base-changed cover on the parameter product, and to its two-parameter product for associativity. The finiteness, projectivity and integrality assertions without a cover are precisely steps 1--4.
